design.md's '### .github/workflows/test.yml (Stream D + Stream A, ONE shared staged batch)' subsection (lines 371-406) and ## Global Constraints (lines 514-520: 'Streams A and D's edits are staged as ONE shared human-copy batch... Stream B does not independently touch test.yml; its CI step is part of the same shared batch') describe only Streams A, B, and D's contributions to the shared test.yml CI-step batch and never mention Stream C's CI-step registration anywhere in the API/Contract Plan or Global Constraints. This contradicts requirements.md's own Non-goals (lines 324-337: 'Stream C registers its runner via the same explicit-step rule, inside this ONE shared batch... its step is no longer deferred to Stream C's own implementation time... leaving it deferred would ship a landed suite with no explicit step, precisely INV-006's silent-skip gap') and AC-019/AC-020 (AC-019 covers 'every new suite from Streams A, B, and C'; AC-020 requires a CI step for every AC-019 suite), and acceptance-tests.md TEST-020 ('the ONE shared batch, Streams A + B + C + D... contains a CI step for each new suite from AC-019 -- Streams A and B, plus Stream C's own tests/workflow-scenarios/workflow-scenarios.tests.sh'). infra-spec.md compounds this with an internal self-contradiction: its opening paragraph (lines 8-14) claims the batch covers 'Streams A/B/C's 3 new CI steps', but its own ## CI/CD Sequence section (lines 45-53) states 'Streams A and B together add exactly 2 new steps' and shows a YAML snippet containing only those 2 steps, omitting Stream C entirely. Failure mode: an implementer following design.md's own contract plan (the concrete, machine-actionable diff specification for the protected test.yml file) would omit Stream C's CI-step registration from the shared human-copy batch, so tests/workflow-scenarios/workflow-scenarios.tests.sh (including the TEST-014 inbound-prompt-injection defense check) would never run in CI -- reproducing exactly the INV-006 silent-registration-gap this feature exists to close, and violating requirements.md's explicit no-deferral instruction. Major: this is a coverage gap likely to cause implementation misalignment and a verification/security exposure (a security-relevant test silently never executing in CI), not a hard policy violation making the design unimplementable.

Reconciled during QG remediation'), none operative. security-spec.md's Security Tests table (lines 108-117) now includes the previously-missing TEST-014 row (B2, inbound prompt injection, RED/GREEN-paired with a pinned defect-count allowlist).
